title: Windows/Linux CI has not run since 2026-05-30: branch 004 is 655 commits ahead of main and the 3-OS workflows only trigger on push:main / pull_request
repro: git log --oneline main..HEAD | wc -l -> 655; gh run list -> newest run 2026-05-30 (main); gh pr list --state all -> only PRs #1/#2 (merged May); branch 004-r4-experience-rebuild is pushed but has no PR, so no windows-latest/ubuntu-latest job has ever built or tested it
evidence: .github/workflows/test.yml:3-6, .github/workflows/build.yml:3-6, .github/workflows/lint.yml:3-6 (push: branches [main] + pull_request only; no workflow_dispatch); gh run list (latest 2026-05-30T19:08Z); git merge-base main HEAD = cfcf5be 2026-05-31
notes: Every static cross-platform claim in this sweep is unverified because the only machine that ran the code since May is this Mac; the CLAUDE.md standard 'builds stay green on Windows, macOS, Linux' is currently unobserved for ~4 months of work (new sidecar deps, curl_cffi --collect-all, new tests). HYG-2 is a proven red Windows pytest that is already waiting. Smallest fix: open a draft PR from the branch (or add workflow_dispatch + a branch push trigger) to get a 3-OS baseline BEFORE the ROG Windows session, so that session starts from a known list instead of discovering build breaks by hand.

title: pytest fixture read with platform-default encoding raises UnicodeDecodeError on Windows (cp1252), turning the windows-latest test job red
repro: python3 -c "open('sidecar/tests/fixtures/saksoft_outcome_pages.json','rb').read().decode('cp1252')" -> UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9d in position 871. On Windows Python 3.13 (UTF-8 mode off, CI sets no PYTHONUTF8), Path.read_text() with no encoding uses cp1252, so the test's fixture load raises before any assertion
evidence: sidecar/tests/test_search_extract.py:463-464 (fixture.read_text() no encoding); sidecar/tests/fixtures/saksoft_outcome_pages.json (139 non-ASCII bytes, en-dashes); .github/workflows/test.yml:77-81 (plain pytest, no PYTHONUTF8); 12 further bare .read_text() calls in tests/ (test_nse_provider.py:27-31, test_corporate_disclosures.py:33-36, test_bse_provider.py:297-298, test_no_tradesa.py:168) are ASCII-only today so latent
notes: Production sidecar code is disciplined here (every open()/read_text()/resources.open() in services/ passes encoding='utf-8'); the tests are not. Consequence: the first 3-OS CI run of this branch (HYG-1) fails on Windows for a reason unrelated to product code, and the next non-ASCII fixture (any Indian filing with an en-dash or rupee sign) adds another. Fix: add encoding='utf-8' to the 13 test reads, or set env PYTHONUTF8: '1' on the pytest step (one line, covers future fixtures).

title: Hardware-fit has no Windows branch: every Windows machine is reported as exactly 8 GiB RAM / 4.4 GiB budget, and the onboarding local-model recommendation is scored against that fiction
repro: cd sidecar && ./.venv/bin/python -c "import platform; from services import hardware_fit as h; platform.system=lambda:'Windows'; print(h.detect_device(force=True).to_dict())" -> ramGib 8.0, gpuBudgetGib 4.4 regardless of the real machine (this Mac has more); GET /system/local-model-recommendation then picks/rejects candidates on that constant
evidence: sidecar/services/hardware_fit.py:203-219 (Darwin -> _detect_macos, Linux -> _detect_linux, else _detect_fallback), sidecar/services/hardware_fit.py:182-197 (_detect_fallback: ram = 8 * _GIB hardcoded), sidecar/services/hardware_fit.py:124-132 (non-Apple: 55% of RAM, dedicated VRAM never detected on Windows or Linux), sidecar/services/hardware_fit.py:86-95 (to_dict emits ramGib with no estimated/provenance flag), sidecar/routers/system.py:106-140
notes: Windows is the operator's primary dev rig and the likeliest non-Mac user platform. A 4 GB laptop is told it has 8 GB (over-recommends a model that will thrash); a 32 GB RTX box is told 8 GB CPU-only (under-recommends, steers to cloud keys). The value is presented as measured, so the user cannot tell. Fix: a _detect_windows via ctypes GlobalMemoryStatusEx (about 15 lines, no new dependency; psutil is not installed), and mark fallback profiles with an estimated flag the UI shows. Dedicated-GPU VRAM (nvidia-smi / DXGI) is a separate, larger follow-up that also affects Linux.

title: The deterministic layout modes (Fundamental / Technical / Macro / Compare / Reset) are reachable only from the macOS native menu; Windows and Linux have no equivalent entry point
repro: On Windows/Linux: install_layout_menu is compiled out, so vysted://menu-layout is never emitted and applyLayoutMode (clear the grid, tile exactly that mode's panels) has no caller. The only non-Mac route is the chat '/layout <name>' slash, which enqueues arrange_layout through the proposed-changes gate and the additive, viewport-fit-downgraded fitLayoutTemplate path, the behaviour the menu bridge was written to avoid ('Bug-4: Fundamental was collapsing to a single brief panel')
evidence: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:344-350 (#[cfg(target_os = "macos")] install_layout_menu, doc: 'Windows/Linux keep their existing chrome untouched'), src-tauri/src/lib.rs:495-500, src/lib/menu-bridge.ts:4-13 and :33 (sole applyLayoutMode caller), src/modules/chat/ChatSidebar.tsx:667-672 (/layout -> enqueueSlashChange('arrange_layout')), src/lib/host-actions.ts:1038-1047 (fitLayoutTemplate)
notes: This is a product surface that exists only on macOS by construction, not by accident of testing. Fix: expose the five modes as command-palette commands that call applyLayoutMode / resetToDefaultLayout directly (platform-neutral, works in every webview), and keep the native menu as macOS sugar that dispatches the same commands. A Settings reset button exists (SettingsPanel.tsx:1593) but only for Reset.

title: Kill-switch global shortcut registers Ctrl+Super+Shift+K (all three modifiers) on every OS, not the documented Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K; on Windows it is Ctrl+Win+Shift+K
repro: Press Ctrl+Shift+K on Windows/Linux, or Cmd+Shift+K on macOS -> nothing fires. The registered chord is Shift|Super|Control+K: global-hotkey 0.7.0 HotKey::new keeps both bits, and the Windows backend maps SUPER->MOD_WIN and CONTROL->MOD_CONTROL into one RegisterHotKey call
evidence: src-tauri/src/kill_switch.rs:34-39 (Modifiers::SHIFT | Modifiers::SUPER | Modifiers::CONTROL), src-tauri/src/kill_switch.rs:20,30,75 (docs and log say Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+K); ~/.cargo/registry/src/*/global-hotkey-0.7.0/src/hotkey.rs:87-99,108-114 and src/platform_impl/windows/mod.rs:77-96; user-facing promise at src/modules/safety/DisclaimerFlow.tsx:45, src/store/safety.ts:14, docs/SAFETY_ARCHITECTURE.md:119,240
notes: A wrong-chord bug on all three OSes, surfaced here because the intent was a per-OS 'CmdOrCtrl'. On Linux Wayland, global-shortcut registration also fails (logged, non-fatal, kill_switch.rs:76-79). Low severity because the kill switch currently gates only broker adapters (subscribers are registered in services/broker_base.py:103,251,345; nothing else subscribes), which the trading removal deletes. Fix alongside that decision: either delete the shortcut with trading, or if the kill switch is kept for agent autonomy, use #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] Modifiers::SUPER, else Modifiers::CONTROL (one line) plus a unit test on the modifier set.

title: Note .md mirror filenames strip only / and \ from a free-text symbol, so Windows-illegal names (NSE:RELIANCE, CON, anything with :*?"<>|) fail silently
repro: On Windows, type 'NSE:RELIANCE' (the TradingView convention) in the notes symbol chip -> filename 'NSE:RELIANCE.md' -> the ':' addresses an NTFS alternate data stream or fails with ERROR_INVALID_NAME in write_text_atomic -> persistNoteMd swallows the error, so the canonical .md never lands; Export .md/.png/.pdf with the same scope shows a raw OS error. A symbol named CON/NUL/AUX/PRN/COM1 hits the reserved-device-name trap
evidence: src/modules/notes/notes-persistence.ts:67-72 (replace(/[/\\]/g,'_') only; empty catch), src/modules/notes/NotesPanel.tsx:220 (exportBaseName, same partial sanitiser), src/modules/notes/NotesPanel.tsx:424-433 (SymbolChipInput: free text, trim + toUpperCase only), src/lib/export-artifact.ts:85,102 and notes-persistence.ts:68 (`${dir}/...` string joins produce mixed separators on Windows, echoed to the user in 'Saved <path>')
notes: No data loss: the workspace blob remains the primary note store. The consequence is a promise (SC-032 durable .md file per note) that quietly does not hold on Windows for some symbols, and two copies of the same sanitiser that can drift apart. Fix: one shared safeFilename() that maps [<>:"/\\|?*\x00-\x1f] to '_', trims trailing dots/spaces and suffixes reserved device names; used by both call sites.

title: The atomic-rename writers have no Windows sharing-violation retry, and the Rust version leaks its temp file when the rename fails
repro: On Windows, os.replace / std::fs::rename -> MoveFileExW(REPLACE_EXISTING) fails with WinError 5/32 when the destination is open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE, for example by Defender or the Search indexer scanning the file just written, or by a concurrent read. Workspace autosave then returns an unhandled 500 (a lost autosave if it was the newest one); a note or export write rejects and leaves '<name>.tmp.<pid>' behind
evidence: sidecar/services/workspace_store.py:85-94 (os.replace, no retry; the tmp is cleaned in finally), sidecar/routers/workspace.py:53-60 (catches only WorkspaceNameError), src-tauri/src/lib.rs:297-309 and :328-341 (std::fs::rename, no retry, no tmp cleanup on error)
notes: The workspace writer was made atomic specifically because concurrent debounced autosaves corrupted JSON (workspace_store.py:72-79); on Windows the fix trades torn files for intermittent PermissionError. Rare, but it lands on the most-written file in the app. Fix: retry the replace 3-5 times with about 50 ms backoff on PermissionError/ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION in both writers, and remove the tmp on rename failure in the Rust commands.

title: MCP supervisors mutate the process environment (set_var/remove_var) from two parallel threads while the GUI and runtime threads are live, which is unsafe on POSIX
repro: design: lib.rs spawns openbb_mcp::spawn and sec_edgar_mcp::spawn on two threads at once; each calls std::env::set_var/remove_var. glibc setenv can reallocate environ while another thread (GTK/WebKitGTK on Linux, tokio workers) runs getenv, which is undefined behaviour and a rare boot-time crash. Rust 2024 made set_var unsafe for exactly this reason; the crate is on edition 2021, so it compiles silently
notes: Windows is unaffected (env access is locked), and macOS/Linux crashes are low-probability. The mechanism exists only to hand the ports to the main sidecar, which is spawned afterwards. Fix: drop the global mutation and pass VYSTED_*_MCP_PORT/HOST with .env(...) on the main sidecar's tauri-plugin-shell Command in start_main_sidecar, reading the ports from the already-managed OpenbbMcpPort/SecEdgarMcpPort state (0 -> omit). This also removes the 'join both threads before the sidecar spawn' ordering constraint (lib.rs:482-485).

title: Hardcoded macOS glyphs in UI hints (⌘K, ⌘B, ⌘↵, ⌘⌫) on every OS, bypassing the platform-aware formatBinding
repro: On Windows the header shows a <kbd>⌘K</kbd> chip and tooltips 'Hide agent panel (⌘B)', 'Accept all (⌘↵)'. A Windows user pressing Win+K opens the OS Cast/Connect flyout. The labels also ignore user rebinding in Settings
evidence: src/app/page.tsx:233, src/app/page.tsx:250-252, src/modules/chat/ProposedChangesReview.tsx:51,59, src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx:1720; the correct helper already exists at src/store/keybindings.ts:281-290 (isMacPlatform) and :328-350 (formatBinding renders Ctrl+K off-Mac)
notes: Functional rather than cosmetic: the hint names a key that does not exist on the platform. The bindings themselves match correctly per OS (keybindings.ts:363-385). Fix: render formatBinding(getBinding('<action>').keys) at the four sites.

title: Sidecar build scripts create the venv from whatever python/python3 is on PATH, with no version check; CI pins 3.13
repro: Fresh Windows: `python` is the Microsoft Store App Execution Alias stub (opens the Store, exit 9009), so `python -m venv` fails with an opaque error. Linux/older macOS: python3 may be 3.11/3.12, which builds a sidecar on a different interpreter than CI (setup-python 3.13) and CLAUDE.md's stated Python 3.13. An existing venv is never re-validated. Separately, `pnpm ci-local` calls bare `python`, which does not exist on this Mac (`which python` -> not found) or stock Ubuntu
notes: This will be the first thing the Windows verification session hits. Fix: on win32 use `py -3.13` (the launcher), on POSIX try python3.13 then python3; after venv creation assert `sys.version_info[:2] == (3, 13)` and fail with a clear message. In ci-local, use the sidecar venv's interpreter.

title: Linux without a Secret Service provider has no credential fallback: release keychain calls error, BYOK keys cannot be saved, and onboarding reappears on every launch
repro: Linux release build on a session with no org.freedesktop.secrets provider (minimal window managers, WSLg, some KDE setups): keyring sync-secret-service errors -> keychain_set rejects (no provider key can be stored) and keychain_get rejects -> onboarding.refresh's catch sets seen:false -> the onboarding flow shows on every boot. A debug build on the same machine waits 140 s in keychain_migrate (a macOS SecurityAgent workaround) because every read errors
evidence: src-tauri/Cargo.toml:35 (only the sync-secret-service backend on Linux), src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:62-89 (os_keychain, no fallback), src-tauri/src/keychain.rs:216-224,280-286 (140 s idle wait, not cfg-gated to macOS), src/store/onboarding.ts:38-54 (a non-secret onboarding flag stored in the secret store), src/lib/keychain.ts:46-54 (app-meta flags documented as non-secrets but kept in the keychain)
notes: GNOME/KDE desktops normally provide the service, hence low. Two cheap parts: keep non-secret app-meta flags (onboarding, ToS timestamps) out of the OS secret store (the workspace blob or a data-dir file), and cfg-gate the 140 s wait to target_os = "macos". The larger decision is whether Linux gets an explicit 'secret store unavailable' error state in KeyEntryDialog rather than a raw invoke rejection.

title: On Windows the whole data dir, including regenerable SQLite caches, goes to Roaming AppData
repro: Tauri app_data_dir resolves to %APPDATA%\com.vysted.terminal (Roaming). The sidecar writes data_cache.db (+ -wal/-shm) and fundamentals_cache.db there (54 MB total on this Mac today). On domain-joined or roaming-profile Windows machines Roaming is synced at logon and logoff, and folder redirection can place it on a network share where SQLite WAL is unsafe
evidence: src-tauri/src/lib.rs:116-134 (resolve_data_dir -> app.path().app_data_dir()), src-tauri/src/lib.rs:142-151, sidecar/config.py:544-549 (single data dir for everything); du of ~/Library/Application Support/com.vysted.terminal = 54M (data_cache.db, fundamentals_cache.db, searxng/, exports/)
notes: This is a cheap decision now and a migration later. Fix shape: keep user state (portfolio, notes, workspaces, audit log) in app_data_dir and pass app_local_data_dir (%LOCALAPPDATA%) as a second --cache-dir for the regenerable caches. Same split on Linux (XDG data vs cache). No effect on macOS behaviour.
